ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Suppose a certain livestock population grazed freely on a grassland shows S-shaped growth, and the trend of the population's growth rate with changes in population size is shown in the figure. If one wants to continuously harvest as much of this livestock as possible, one should begin capturing when the population size is appropriate. Among the following four population sizes, which is appropriate?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the horizontal axis is labeled "population size" and the vertical axis is labeled "population growth rate". The curve is single-peaked: it rises as population size increases from near the origin, reaches a maximum point, and then falls. Among the four labels, Jia is located at a lower point on the rising section, Yi is located at a higher point on the rising section, Bing is close to the position of maximum growth rate, and Ding is located on the descending section after the peak, on the right side where the population size is larger. Reasoning: When this livestock population shows S-shaped growth, the population growth rate is greatest near K/2. To continuously harvest as much as possible, the population size after capture should be maintained near K/2, so as to maintain the maximum growth rate and thereby obtain the maximum sustainable yield. Therefore, when capture begins, the population size should be slightly higher than K/2, that is, at a position to the right of the maximum growth-rate point with a larger population size. In the figure, the vicinity of Bing corresponds to the maximum growth rate, and Ding is to its right with a larger population size, making it suitable as the population size at which to begin capture.
